questions.q: Why can an AI assistant state something false with complete confidence?
options: It is designed to mislead people who ask tricky questions
It copies the first web page it finds without checking it
It predicts the most plausible reply instead of retrieving verified facts
It only makes mistakes when a conversation is very short
questions.explain: AI writes answers by predicting the most plausible next words, so when it lacks a specific fact, plausible-sounding text can still be wrong, and it sounds just as confident.

questions.q: An assistant gives you a list of books with authors and years. What's the smartest step before you buy one?
options: Ask it to rate its confidence in each item, then search the flagged titles
Trust the list, since a confident tone means the details are accurate
Ask "Isn't this a great list?" so it confirms the details are right
Keep the same chat open for weeks so it remembers the list for you
questions.explain: Titles, authors and years are the kind of specifics where hallucinations cluster. A confidence self-rating surfaces the shakiest items, and a quick search for each settles it.

questions.q: You want honest feedback on a plan you're excited about. Which question is most likely to get it?
options: Why will this plan work so well?
Don't you agree this plan is ready?
What are the weaknesses in this plan?
questions.explain: Assistants are built to be agreeable, so leading questions invite agreement. Asking directly for weaknesses gets a more honest, useful answer.
